steps.description: The girl pauses suddenly, bringing both hands to Katakamukha near the ears/cheeks, expressing dawning realization and concern.
steps.rasa_expression: Eyes widen slightly (Vismaya), then quickly drop to look at the ankle with a look of worry (light Karuna).
steps.teaching_note: The transition to stillness must be sharp; utilize a subtle, quick weight shift (Kampa) to show nervous thought.

steps.description: Hands open into Alapadma and are held at chest level while the head turns quickly left and right (Parivartita and Prasarita Shiras) to scan the surroundings.
steps.rasa_expression: Quick, restless glances (Chalanadrishthi) left and right, expressing mounting anxiety.
steps.teaching_note: Ensure the head movement is separate from the torso; the body must remain stable in Araimandi during the search.

steps.description: A slow, controlled turn to the Left side (180 degrees) on two beats, right hand in Pataka extended outwards (searching motion).
steps.rasa_expression: A sighing look (Nishvasa) of slight despair (Karuna) as the immediate search proves fruitless.
steps.teaching_note: The turn must be smooth and steady (Lathā Mudrā-like); avoid an abrupt pivot to sustain the intermediate grace.

steps.description: A controlled turn back to the Front (180 degrees) on two beats, eyes scanning the floor as the body returns to the starting axis.
steps.rasa_expression: The gaze is focused downwards (Adhomukha) intently, meticulously searching the immediate floor area.
steps.teaching_note: Ensure the return turn is balanced and centered, maintaining the Araimandi without rising.

steps.description: A sudden, quick drop into Muzhumandi (Mandi posture), right hand in Pataka points directly at the floor in front of the foot.
steps.rasa_expression: A sharp, focused light in the eyes (Adbhuta) that instantly locks onto the object; the mouth opens in a small 'O' shape.
steps.teaching_note: The drop must be executed cleanly and sharply on the single beat; the shift in focus and expression must be immediate and dramatic.

steps.description: The right hand switches to Alapadma (to 'pick up' the anklet) and is slowly brought up towards the ear, hands held near the head/ear.
steps.rasa_expression: A relieved, happy smile spreads across the face, followed by a soft, grateful look (Adbhuta/Karuna turning to Shanta).
steps.teaching_note: Maintain the low Mandi posture throughout the lift; the movement of the arm should be deliberate, showing care for the retrieved object.
